newsitem.title: USA: Aero Flight Services grounded by U.S. regulators.
newsitem.headline: Aero Flight Services grounded by U.S. regulators.

text.p: The Federal Aviation Administration on Friday said it issued an emergency order revoking the operating certificate of Aero Flight Services Inc of Fort Lauderdale, Fla.

The FAA said the order was based on evidence that the carrier improperly converted four Hawker-Siddley aircraft from passenger to cargo configuration and made other major alterations that were performed "contrary to FAA-approved engineering data."
The regulators said Aero Flight failed to keep accurate records and returned planes to service "even though they did not meet FAA certification requirements."
"As a result, the aircraft were not airworthy when operated in cargo service," the FAA said.
The FAA also accused the carrier of skipping or improperly performing maintenance and violating rules governing the shipment of hazardous materials.
The FAA said the carrier operated four aircraft in on-demand service, air ambulance and cargo flights.
A woman who answered the phone at the company's Fort Lauderdale office said she knew nothing of the FAA action and that no one there could comment.
